correctness.rationale: For every n≥1, the count q_{n,k}=k(n)_k/n^{k+1} follows from the rooted-forest formula and a uniform permutation on the cyclic set; inclusion-exclusion gives the rencontres law and the independent-image model gives the binomial fixed-point marginal. Their mixture produces an exact finite-n TV formula. The conditional fixed-point expectation equals one, proving zero covariance, while K_n=1 proves dependence for n≥2. A dominating summable sequence kδ_k justifies passing the limit through the mixture. The alternating Taylor remainder sums exactly to (3e²+1)/8, and a factorial-tail-controlled binomial-to-Poisson expansion gives 3/(4e). Direct exact enumeration through n=6 and a numerical series check support the analytic proof; they are not used as infinite certificates.

originality.rationale: The known decomposition of a random endofunction into cyclic permutation and rooted forest makes the finite joint law classical, and this is not claimed as the advance. The inspected 2022 mapping-cycle study, 2010 cyclic-point-conditioned mapping paper, and fixed-point-marked mapping enumeration do not state the sharp first-order total-variation dependence asymptotic with constant ((3e^2+1)/8+3/(4e)). The proof supplies a new summable rencontres-discrepancy calculation and retains the marginal binomial correction. Broader historical-priority risk remains from general mapping enumeration and older Poisson-approximation literature; this is a self-review, not independent certification.
residual_risks: The foundational 1990 Flajolet–Odlyzko treatment was only bibliographically accessible, so it may imply an equivalent first-order dependence constant.
Earlier permutation Poisson-approximation or mapping marked-generating-function literature may explicitly contain the same closed constant under a different dependence metric.
Finite joint probabilities are classical; novelty and value depend specifically on the analytic extraction of the sharp product-marginal total-variation constant.

value.rationale: The pair of fixed points and cyclic vertices is a canonical local/global pair of statistics of random functional digraphs. Exact zero covariance conceals genuine finite dependence. Its sharp TV asymptotic quantifies operational asymptotic independence at the natural 1/n scale, with a nontrivial explicit constant split into rare conditioned-permutation errors and a marginal Poissonization correction. This is meaningful even though the exact finite joint law is classical.
